title: Activepieces vs Gumloop? Which to Choose in 2026
summary: Activepieces vs Gumloop: see which automation tool suits different workflows and budgets. Understand pricing and features to choose the right one.
body_markdown:
## When self-hosting, licensing, and embedding apply


If your data has to stay on servers you run, or your customers need automation inside your own product, Activepieces covers both: it self-hosts from an MIT-licensed core, and its embedded flow builder places automation inside your application.


A hosted-only canvas isn't built to do either.


### Self-hosting and licence


Because Activepieces is open source, you can read the code, run it on your own infrastructure and keep every workflow and credential inside your network.


The practical consequence is a cost shape that differs from a per-seat or per-task bill: you pay for the server and for whoever keeps it patched, upgraded and backed up.


For a bootstrapped team with one capable engineer, that trade is often cheaper and easier to defend. For a team with nobody to own it, it's a chore that lands on the wrong person at the wrong time.


Gumloop's documentation describes a hosted product that you use through Gumloop's own cloud. Check its docs for any dedicated or private deployment option before you assume one exists.


If a data-residency rule forces the tool onto your own machines, the usual worry is that the self-hosted build is a stripped-down copy of the cloud.


With Activepieces the air-gapped edition carries SSO, SCIM, custom RBAC, audit logs, release management and secret managers, the same list as the managed cloud, and regulated and public-sector organisations already run it in production. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces as well.


Self-hosted enterprise setups go through the sales form:[https://www.activepieces.com/sales](https://www.activepieces.com/sales)


### Embedding in your own product


Your customers can build and run automations without leaving your interface or creating an account with a third party, because Activepieces lets you place its flow builder inside your own application.


That matters if automation is a feature you sell, because the alternative is sending customers to someone else's login screen and handing over a slice of the relationship.


It also means you carry the maintenance of that integration, so budget engineering time for it.


Embedding's a sales-led conversation, and the same form's where to start:[https://www.activepieces.com/sales](https://www.activepieces.com/sales)


Gumloop's docs position it as a workspace for your own team to build in. Read them for any embedding or white-label offer before you plan around one.


### Security and SOC 2 status compared


Many security reviews are really asking where data lives and who can reach it, and self-hosting gives you control over both.


**Activepieces isn't SOC 2 certified** ; that programme's in progress. If a certificate's a hard procurement requirement today, say so to sales early and ask what evidence they can supply in its place.


Read Gumloop's own security documentation for its current compliance statements rather than relying on a summary.
